concepts.name: Trie Fundamentals
concepts.mental_model: An org-chart/subway map growing down from a blank root. A word is a PATH from the root, not a stored string; you know a path spells a real word because its landing node has flag=True.
concepts.mnemonic: Index is the letter, flag is the finish line. (val[ord(ch)-ord('a')] = the child; flag = a word ends here.)

concepts.name: Insertion
concepts.mental_model: Walk the word from root, one node per letter; conjure a child only when the slot is empty; set flag on the last node.
concepts.mnemonic: Index, walk-or-create, finish line. The advance (ptr = ptr.val[idx]) is unconditional; only creation is conditional.

concepts.name: Exact Search
concepts.mental_model: Re-walk the word; a missing slot means 'not here' -> return False. Land on the last node and READ its flag (don't just confirm arrival).
concepts.mnemonic: Same walk as insert, but missing slot = dead end, and the finish line must be lit: return ptr.flag.

past_mistakes.note: LC-720 variant: when the check needs flag=True at EVERY prefix node, advance FIRST then read ptr.flag; reading before advancing tests the parent and hits root.flag=False on iteration 1. Resolved 2026-09-19 by tracing helper('a').

concepts.name: Prefix Search
concepts.mental_model: Identical walk to search, but the path merely existing is enough. No flag check — return True if you survived the walk.
concepts.mnemonic: startsWith = 'did the road exist', search = 'and is there a house at the end'. Only search reads the flag.

concepts.name: Word Search / Wildcards
concepts.mental_model: Reframe search as recursive DFS(node, i) = 'can word[i:] match starting from node?'. A '.' forks into all children; a single walking pointer can't branch, so recursion is the shape.
concepts.mnemonic: Dot = fork (any child), letter = one road, end of word = read the flag. any() over children short-circuits on first hit.

past_mistakes.note: First wildcard attempt used an iterative single-ptr loop: iterated dict KEYS not children, recursed from self.root instead of the current child, didn't consume the dot (word[idx:] vs idx+1), and fell through to ptr.val['.'] (KeyError). Root cause: tried to express branching without recursion. SOLUTION WAS PROVIDED (learner asked) — needs to re-implement solo to earn mastery.

Solo re-implementation attempt (2026-09-20) still had: (a) dot quantifier INVERTED — 'if not dfs(child): return False' (all-must-match) instead of 'if dfs(child): return True / else return False after loop' (any-can-match); (b) kept pre-filled 52-key dict so 'ch not in node.val' never fires and .values() yields Nones -> crash; (c) 'nb' typo. Solution provided a SECOND time. Must produce the 4-case DFS skeleton cold next session before this counts as mastered.
